Commentary.Commentary: We are back with the chase. The English players are out in the middle taking their respective field positions. Michael van Lingen and Niko Davin will be the openers for Namibia. Reece Topley will bowl the first over for England.
... The Run Chase ...

English batter Jonny Bairstow is up for a quick chat and says that it was a difficult pitch to bat on but the side did well to close the game on a high and post a good total on board. Mentions that David Wiese bowled really well but they'll look to defend the total set by them. Adds that there was swing on offer and with the covers being placed for such a while it was obvious that the pitch would be sweating a bit and it did. Credits Harry Brook for his brilliant batting and says that it is simple with Brook as they just have to let him bat and set him free.

The bowling from Namibia was good to begin with but they lost their way after the 3rd over. David Wiese in particular was superb as he bowled 2 overs for 6 and took 1 wicket as well. Merwe Erasmus and Jack Brassell were costly and gave away 58 off their 4 overs. Ruben Trumpelmann took 2 wickets while Bernard Scholtz took one as well. With the ball holding in the surface and the wet outfield leveling things this is going to be an exciting chase.

After being asked to bat first, England got off to a rocky start as they lost their openers cheaply and found it difficult to score freely to start with. The arrival of Jonny was key for England as he took on the bowlers from the opposition and managed to up the scoring rate. Jonny Bairstow along with Harry Brook managed to score 56 for the third wicket and set the tone for the others to follow. After the dismissal of Jonny Bairstow, It was Harry Brook and Moeen Ali who knitted a quickfire partnership of 38 runs that helped the side massively in closing their innings on a higher note. Harry Brook was the top scorer as he scored 47 off just 20 deliveries. Jonny Bairstow too played a good knock of 31. Moeen Ali and Liam Livingstone played good cameos as well.

In a rain-curtailed game, the English side has posted a good score on board. With a blistering knock from Jonny Bairstow and Harry Brook the defending champions have posted 122 on board. The revised target though for Namibia would be 126.

Commentary.Commentary: We are ready to start. The umpires have made their way into the middle followed by the players of Namibia, who take their respective field positions. Phil Salt and Jos Buttler walk out as the openers for England. David Wiese will bowl the first over for Namibia.
It is time for the pre-match formalities. The teams are out for their respective national anthems. It will England's first followed by the national anthem of Namibia.

The skipper of England Jos Buttler says it was frustrating but he is delighted they have a game. Informs they have two changes, Jacks and Wood miss out and Curran and Jordan come in. They have made the changes keeping the conditions in mind. Ends by saying every team is dangerous.

The skipper of Namibia Merwe Erasmus has won the coin flip and he says it is a shortened game and hence, wants to bowl. Adds that batting second they could control the game better. Informs they have one change as JP Kotze comes in for Ben Shikongo.
England (Playing XI) - Phil Salt, Jos Buttler (C)(WK), Jonny Bairstow, Harry Brook, Moeen Ali, Liam Livingstone, Sam Curran, Chris Jordan, Jofra Archer, Adil Rashid, Reece Topley.
Namibia (Playing XI) - Niko Davin, Michael van Lingen, Jan Frylinck, JP Kotze, Merwe Erasmus (C), JJ Smit, David Wiese, Zane Green (WK), Ruben Trumpelmann, Bernard Scholtz, Jack Brassell.

Saying that, Namibia are a dangerous side, they have a few special players but they haven't been at their best so far in this tournament. However, they would love to play as party spoilers here. They'll have to be at their best if they are to beat this strong England side. Can they upset the odds?

The World Cup continues and it has been nothing short of entertaining. We now welcome you to the coverage of another game which has a lot depending on it. First, it is a must-win for England. Their previous win has given their net run rate a massive boost and another win like that will see them move above Scotland who will be facing the Aussies. England's qualification thoigh totally depends on that game but they would be hoping to do their job and that is end the group stage with a win and they'll surely be backing themselves to do so.
... MATCH DAY ...

The T20 cricket festival is in full swing as we await match number 34 of the 2024 T20 Men's World Cup. The clash will occur in Sir Vivian Richards Stadium in Antigua where England and Namibia lock horns against each other. We are nearing the end of the group stages and each team wants to qualify for the Super 8 stages and be alive in the tournament. Namibia are officially out of the qualification scenario and this match might be a formality for them but England have a lot riding on this. With 3 points they are stranded at third on their table with Scotland above them with 5 points. England desperately needs to win this and a healthy margin would be gracefully accepeted by the English side and they'd hope that Australia beat Scotland. They were lethal in their last game against Oman. They didn't allow any of their batters to settle in. Adil bagged 4 wickets while Archer and Wood grabbed 3 each. They bowled out Oman for a mere 47 runs, which was an easy target to chase. The batters too didn't fail to in their task and attacked from the first ball. They lost two wickets but the aggressive batting of Jos made it possible to chase the target down in just 3.1 overs hence boosting their NRR by a long margin. Namibia on the other hand had a poor tournament. They failed to win a single match until now and couldn't perform as expected. Against the Aussies, they were bowled out for just 72 runs with their skipper, Gerhard being the top scorer with 36 to his name. Apart from him, only Michael got his score to the double digits. The bowlers didn't have much to defend either and apart from the wicket by David, they couldn't find any success. They have a chance to win their second match of the tournament and also spoil the party for the English. Which team are you supporting?
